newsitem.title: QATAR: Korea Gas Corp sees growing LNG imports.
newsitem.headline: Korea Gas Corp sees growing LNG imports.

text.p: South Korean liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports will rise to 20.7 million tonnes in the year 2001 from 9.5 million tonnes last year, vice-president of Korea Gas Corp (KOGAS) Young-Jin Kwon said on Tuesday.

LNG import demand, fired by an expanded domestic gas network, growing industrial use and environmental regulation, would hit 25 million tonnes in 2006 and 29.3 tonnes in 2010, Kwon said in a paper delivered to a gas conference in Qatar.
South Korea is seen as one of the fastest growing areas of natural gas demand growth with total demand reaching 28.5 tonnes by 2010 versus 9.3 million tonnes last year.
KOGAS imports LNG from Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei and Australia and is set to take deliveries from Gulf Arab Qatar in 1999 and Oman in the following year.

This left KOGAS needing to secure an additional seven million tonnes over existing supply contracts for deliveries in 2001, 11.2 million tonnes for 2006 and 17.8 million tonnes in 2010, Kwon told delegates.
KOGAS was looking at pipeline supplies of Russian gas to cover part of the short-fall, Kwon said.
